title: 2012 HMMT February Geometry Problem 1
statement: \(A B C\) is an isosceles triangle with \(A B=2\) and \(\measuredangle A B C=90^{\circ} . D\) is the midpoint of \(B C\) and \(E\) is on \(A C\) such that the area of \(A E D B\) is twice the area of \(E C D\). Find the length of \(D E\).

solutions.text: \(\frac{\sqrt{17}}{3}\) Let \(F\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(E\) to \(B C\). We have \([A E D B]+[E D C]=\) \([A B C]=2 \Rightarrow[E D C]=\frac{2}{3}\). Since we also have \([E D C]=\frac{1}{2}(E F)(D C)\), we get \(E F=F C=\frac{4}{3}\). So \(F D=\frac{1}{3}\), and \(E D=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{3}\) by the Pythagorean Theorem.
